title: Find the project file from a subdirectory: resolve .engram-project by searching the working directory's ancestors
outcome: Find the project file from a subdirectory: resolve .engram-project by searching the working directory's ancestors
acceptance: When no --project-file is given, the CLI and MCP resolve the project by walking from the working directory up through its ancestors to the nearest .engram-project, stopping at the filesystem root. An explicit --project-file still wins.
A refusal when no project file is found anywhere on the path names the directory searched from and the remedy, and never suggests creating a new .engram-project in a subdirectory.

Tests cover: resolution from a nested subdirectory of a repository; a nested different project (the nearest file wins); a linked worktree inside the repository; an explicit --project-file overriding the search; and the not-found refusal.
The docs (README setup and cli-and-mcp.md) state the resolution rule.

completion.summary: CLI and MCP select the nearest .engram-project by walking cwd ancestors to the filesystem root, with explicit project-file override and no fallback on invalid markers. Refusal names search origin and existing marker remedy. Nested/nearest/linked-worktree/override/not-found tests and docs delivered. Full nine-stage Windows gate, Codex/Claude whole-input pair, independent four-criterion acceptance, and readiness of four live stores passed. Installed clean release and verified origin/master push; marker type/size robustness Low tracked separately.
